purpose: Test whether a conventional one-amplitude angular lens-potential multipole can reproduce the spent-data gain attributed to the rejected gas-minus-star transport flux.

control_fields.phase_provenance: gas centroid minus stellar centroid axis measured in P0607 before P0648; no image position sets phase
control_fields.radial_scale_provenance: fixed broad cluster-core scale, not fit
control_fields.normalization_provenance: P0646 gas-minus-star unit field RMS over the identical grid

cross_validation.fold_definition: reuse exact P0645 five source-family-stratified folds
cross_validation.selection_metric: pooled exact CV RMS with complete roots
cross_validation.tie_break: lower absolute amplitude, then signed amplitude

predeclared_interpretation.candidate_specificity_survives_definitio: P0647 boundary candidate CV RMS is at least 1 percent lower than every root-complete exact multipole control
predeclared_interpretation.generic_angular_control_explains_gain_de: a root-complete exact multipole control is within 1 percent of or below the P0647 boundary candidate CV RMS
predeclared_interpretation.multipole_amplitude_identified_definitio: the best exact multipole amplitude is not an endpoint of the signed grid

claim_boundary: All image-position scores are from spent RX J2129 data.
The multipoles are conventional scalar-potential controls, not physical baryonic mass models.
Phase, radial scale, taper, support, and normalization are fixed; only one signed amplitude changes.
P0647 already rejected the unbounded component-flux family; P0648 tests specificity and does not reopen it.
No P0633 or P0640 validation outcome may be opened.
